title: SOC 2 vs. ISO 27001: Navigating the 93 Controls
metaDescription: Deciding between SOC 2 and ISO 27001? Discover how ISO's 93 controls map to SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria to streamline dual-framework compliance audits.
excerpt: Choosing between SOC 2 and ISO 27001 doesn't have to be an either-or dilemma. Explore how to harmonize ISO's 93 Annex A controls with SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria.
content:
When enterprise prospects review your security posture, the conversation inevitably circles back to proof of assurance: Do you hold a SOC 2 Type II report, or are you ISO/IEC 27001 certified? As organizations face mounting supply chain security scrutiny in 2026, compliance officers frequently struggle to decide which framework should take priority—or whether they must tackle both simultaneously. A recent breakdown by Tech Insider highlighted the enduring friction between these two standards, focusing particularly on how the modern 93 Annex A controls in ISO 27001 align with the AICPA’s Trust Services Criteria.

Attestation vs. Certification: The Fundamental Divide

While both frameworks demonstrate a robust cybersecurity posture, their structural mechanics differ significantly. SOC 2 is not a certification; it is an independent attestation governed by the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants (AICPA). Conducted by licensed CPA firms, a SOC 2 Type II report evaluates whether your controls operated effectively over a defined observation window—typically six to twelve months.

Conversely, ISO 27001 is a globally recognized, certifiable international standard governed by the International Organization for Standardization. It demands an Information Security Management System (ISMS) anchored around leadership commitment, continuous risk treatment, and standardized operational controls. ISO 27001 certification lasts for a three-year cycle supported by annual surveillance audits.

For organizations operating primarily in North America, SaaS buyers overwhelmingly demand SOC 2. However, for multinational expansion across EMEA and APAC, ISO 27001 remains the baseline prerequisite for enterprise procurement.

Mapping ISO's 93 Controls to SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria

The consolidation of ISO 27001 controls into 93 specific safeguards categorized into four distinct themes—Organizational (37), People (8), Physical (14), and Technological (34)—offers a clear blueprint for compliance mapping. The vast majority of these safeguards map directly to the SOC 2 Common Criteria (CC series):

  • Access Control & Identity: Technological control 8.5 (Secure authentication) and organizational control 5.15 (Access control) correlate directly to SOC 2 CC6.1, CC6.2, and CC6.3.
  • Change Management & System Development: Controls 8.25 through 8.32 map seamlessly to SOC 2 CC8.1, demanding documented test results, peer code reviews, and separation of development and production environments.
  • Threat Detection & Incident Management: Control 8.16 (Monitoring activities) and control 5.24 (Incident response planning) fulfill CC7.2 and CC7.3 monitoring and response mandates.
  • Vendor Risk Management: Annex A controls 5.19 through 5.22 address supplier relationships, mirroring the stringent vendor oversight requirements found under SOC 2 CC9.2.

Crucially, this control architecture also builds substantial cross-framework momentum for other regulatory baselines. The evidence gathered across physical, technological, and identity domains creates near-total coverage for the HIPAA Security Rule's administrative and technical safeguards, while establishing foundational alignment with CMMC Level 2 (NIST SP 800-171) domains.

Executing a Unified Audit Evidence Strategy

Rather than managing two fragmented audit workstreams, forward-thinking compliance officers build a single controls matrix. The key challenge lies in satisfying differing audit methodologies:

  1. Bridge Point-in-Time with Historical Population: ISO 27001 auditors evaluate the maturity and process adherence of your ISMS, whereas SOC 2 auditors pull statistical sample populations across your observation window. Ensure that your automated logging captures timestamps, approvals, and reviewer identities continuously without retrospection gaps.
  2. Standardize Evidence Workspaces: Centralize artifacts such as vulnerability scans, patch management verification logs, and annual penetration tests so the same artifact satisfies ISO control 8.8 and SOC 2 CC7.1.
  3. Align Scope and Boundary Definitions: Keep your system boundaries uniform. If cloud environments or third-party contractors are in scope for SOC 2's Confidentiality or Availability criteria, maintain consistent boundaries across your Statement of Applicability (SoA) for ISO 27001.

Streamlining Your Enterprise Assurance Roadmap

The choice between SOC 2 and ISO 27001 is rarely binary in modern enterprise SaaS. By leveraging the structured layout of the 93 Annex A controls, compliance teams can build a defensible security posture that satisfies international standards while supplying the historical operational evidence required for SOC 2 Type II reports. To eliminate manual collection overhead and maintain continuous compliance across SOC 2, HIPAA, and federal frameworks, modern teams often rely on automation partners like Espresso Labs to bridge the operational gap between IT management and audit readiness. Treat compliance as continuous operational hygiene rather than an annual scramble, and the 93 controls will serve as an accelerator for revenue rather than an administrative bottleneck.
